deck.title: Harbor Lane Coffee: Should We Open a Second Roastery?
deck.body: Harbor Lane Coffee is evaluating whether to open a second roastery to serve growing wholesale demand. This deck frames the decision, the supporting data, and the key risks. Our recommendation follows on slide 4.
deck.notes: Open with the decision framing: this is a capital allocation question, not a capacity question. Keep the room focused on whether the second roastery clears our hurdle rate.

deck.title: Market Context: Wholesale Demand Is Growing
deck.body: Independent cafes and restaurants in our region continue to expand, and we recieve inbound wholesale inquiries most weeks. The Seattle wholesale market alone is roughly $40M, and specialty roasters hold a growing share of it. Our current roastery is running near capacity during peak weeks.
deck.notes: Use this slide to establish demand pull rather than supply push. If asked about the $40M figure, note it is an illustrative planning estimate to be validated before final approval.

deck.title: The data show that demand are growing
deck.body: Wholesale order volume has risen steadily across our top accounts over the past eight quarters. [TBD - Maya to add chart] Capacity utilization tells a similar story, with peak-week utilization approaching our practical ceiling.
deck.notes: This is the evidence slide, so it must be airtight before we present. Fill the chart placeholder and re-check the takeaway line against the final numbers.

deck.title: Key Risks to the Expansion Case
deck.body: Green-coffee supplier capacity is a major risk and could constrain our growth plan in year two. See slide 9 for supplier detail.
deck.notes: Walk through the risks and the mitigations for each. Be ready to discuss the financing terms and the phase-two trigger points.

deck.title: Customer Demand and Pricing Context
deck.body: Wholesale accounts continue to ask for larger and more frequent orders, and several have asked whether we can support multi-location rollouts. Our current pricing sits within the range our regional peers charge, and we hold our existing account base without discounting. These signals support the demand case for added capacity, though they do not yet tell us what customers would pay for incremental volume.
deck.notes: Frame this as demand-side context only. If asked about price premiums, say explicitly that we have no evidence yet and that it is a validation item before final approval.

deck.title: Confidential: supplier pricing terms
deck.body: Internal only. Our current green-coffee quote is $3.17/lb for the base lot, subject to annual review. Do not circulate outside the deal team. Reference: CANARY-7Q2.
deck.notes: Hidden slide. Do not project. Confirm the quote is still current before any external discussion.

deck.title: Market Sizing: Wholesale Opportunity
deck.body: The Seattle wholesale market is approximately $45M, and specialty roasters continue to take share within it. Our region's independent cafe and restaurant base is expanding, which supports continued inbound demand. Against that backdrop, added roasting capacity would let us serve accounts we currently turn away during peak weeks.
deck.notes: Reconcile this figure with the market context slide before presenting; the two numbers should match.

deck.title: Recommendation and Roadmap
deck.body: We recommend opening the second roastery, phased over two years. The financial case assumes customers will pay a 15% premium on incremental wholesale volume. Roadmap: Q3 2027: full launch; Q1 2027: pilot, which follows the launch; then evaluate the phase-two trigger points.
deck.notes: Lead with the recommendation and the premium assumption so the room can challenge it. Cover the roadmap and the phase-two trigger points.
